source.objectiveEnglishInternal: give a specific, natural compliment and thank the staff warmly
source.roleplayEnglishInternal: Tell the cook why the pastry or coffee was memorable rather than only saying it was good.

readerVerbExamples.target: Felicito al cocinero por el desayuno.
readerVerbExamples.native: I compliment the cook on the breakfast.
I am very grateful to you for the service.

readerVerbExamples.target: Recomiendo este café a mis amigos.
readerVerbExamples.native: I recommend this coffee to my friends.

archivedDraft.scene: After breakfast, Sam thanks café staff for a coffee and pastry.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: メキシコ風の甘いパン

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: I want to compliment you on the breakfast.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 朝食がすばらしかったとお伝えしたいです。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I want to tell you that the breakfast was wonderful.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: El café estaba delicioso, justo como me gusta.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: The coffee was delicious, just the way I like it.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: コーヒーはおいしくて、ちょうど私好みでした。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The coffee was delicious and exactly to my taste.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Me encantó porque estaba muy suave.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: I loved it because it was very soft.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: とてもやわらかかったので、すごく気に入りました。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Because it was very soft, I liked it very much.

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Thank you very much for the service.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 接客していただき、本当にありがとうございました。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Thank you very much for serving me.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Si regreso mañana, voy a pedir otro.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: If I come back tomorrow, I'm going to order another one.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 明日また来たら、もう一つ注文します。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: If I come again tomorrow, I will order one more.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Una viajera termina su desayuno en un café pequeño y quiere hablar con el cocinero.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: A traveler finishes her breakfast in a small café and wants to talk to the cook.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者の女性は、小さなカフェで朝食を食べ終え、料理人と話したいと思っています。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: A female traveler finishes her breakfast at a small café and wants to talk with the cook.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Ella lo saluda y dice: Quiero felicitarlo por el desayuno.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: She greets him and says: I want to compliment you on the breakfast.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 彼女は彼にあいさつをして言います。「朝食がすばらしかったとお伝えしたいです。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: She greets him and says: 'I want to tell you that the breakfast was wonderful.'

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El café estaba muy fuerte y tenía un aroma delicioso, justo como me gusta.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The coffee was very strong and had a delicious aroma, just the way I like it.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 「コーヒーはとても濃くて、香りがすばらしく、ちょうど私好みでした。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The coffee was very strong, its aroma was wonderful, and it was exactly to my taste.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El pan dulce estaba suave por dentro y crujiente por fuera, y no era demasiado dulce.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The sweet bread was soft inside and crunchy outside, and it wasn't too sweet.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 「甘いパンは中はやわらかく、外はカリッとしていて、甘すぎませんでした。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The sweet bread was soft inside, crisp outside, and not too sweet.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: También me encantaron los huevos, porque estaban cremosos y muy bien sazonados.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I also loved the eggs, because they were creamy and very well seasoned.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 「卵もクリーミーで味つけがとてもよかったので、すごく気に入りました。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I also liked the eggs very much because they were creamy and very well seasoned.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El cocinero sonríe y explica que el pan dulce es una receta de su abuela.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The cook smiles and explains that the sweet bread is his grandmother's recipe.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 料理人はにっこり笑って、その甘いパンは自分の祖母のレシピだと説明します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The cook smiles and explains that the sweet bread is his grandmother's recipe.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La viajera le dice: Si regreso mañana, voy a pedir otro de esos.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The traveler tells him: If I come back tomorrow, I'm going to order another one of those.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は彼に言います。「明日また来たら、あのパンをもう一つ注文します。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler tells him: 'If I come again tomorrow, I will order one more of that bread.'

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Antes de salir, deja una propina en el mostrador y da las gracias al personal por la atención.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Before leaving, she leaves a tip on the counter and thanks the staff for the service.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店を出る前に、彼女はカウンターにチップを置き、スタッフに接客のお礼を言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Before leaving the shop, she places a tip on the counter and thanks the staff for the service.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El cocinero responde: Muchas gracias, nos alegra mucho que le haya gustado.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The cook answers: Thank you very much, we're so glad you liked it.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 料理人は答えます。「どうもありがとうございます。気に入っていただけて、私たちはとてもうれしいです。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The cook answers: 'Thank you very much. We are very glad you liked it.'

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Give a specific compliment about the breakfast and thank the cook and staff.
speakingGoalInternal: Tell the cook why the pastry or coffee was memorable rather than only saying it was good.
sourceConflictInternal: The current source Reader follows a female traveler thanking a male cook after strong coffee, Mexican sweet bread, creamy seasoned eggs and a grandmother recipe, then leaving a tip on the counter. The archived Japanese draft instead follows Sam thanking staff for coffee and generic pastry and omits those source details.

savedPositionPolicy: Archived draft rows have no explicit stable row IDs and were not registered. Revision-scoped candidate IDs do not authorize saved-item or audio placement migration. Reordering requires a new revision.
reviewQuestionsInternal: The source is a Mexican café scene. Keep pan dulce and the tip on the counter as scene facts; qualified Japanese and Mexican-food review should check メキシコ風の甘いパン as a descriptive label.
Card 13 and Reader 2 render a direct compliment as 朝食がすばらしかった; qualified Japanese review should decide the most natural customer-to-cook phrasing.
The term 接客 covers service in this café context but is narrower than all uses of Spanish atención; dictionary review should pin the sense.
Card 18 says another one without a referent, as the source card does; Reader 7 names the bread. Preserve this card/Reader difference until source review.
The source note felicitarlo/felicitarla is a Spanish gender contrast. It is internal source context, not a Japanese form rule.
Check whether the Japanese coffee description distinguishes the card's deliciousness from the Reader's strong aromatic coffee.
Check all 27 Japanese faces and literal glosses with a qualified Japanese reviewer before any audio or learner use.
